text: If you see your brother's ox or his sheep straying, do not ignore it; be sure to take it back to him.
If your brother does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, take the animal home with you and keep it until he comes looking for it; then give it back to him.
Do the same with his donkey, and the same with his cloak, and the same with anything else your brother loses and you find. You must not ignore it.
If you see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road, do not ignore it; help him get the animal back on its feet.
A woman must not put on a man's clothing, and a man must not wear a woman's garment, for whoever does such things is detestable to the LORD your God.
If you come upon a bird's nest along the road, in a tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs and the mother sitting on them, do not take the mother along with the young.
You must let the mother go and take only the young, so that it may go well with you and you may live long.
When you build a new house, put a railing around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if someone should fall from it.

Do not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield will be forfeit—both the crop you have sown and the fruit of the vineyard.[^1]

[^1]: Literally "become holy," that is, set apart so that the owner may no longer use it.

versions.text: Do not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield will be forfeit—both the crop you have sown and the fruit of the vineyard.
versions.explanation: The rendering "forfeit" is a reasonable interpretation of the Hebrew verb "become holy/consecrated," but a brief footnote would help the reader understand the underlying idiom without altering the readable text.

text: Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
Do not wear cloth of mixed fibers, wool and linen woven together.
Make tassels for the four corners of the cloak you wrap around yourself.
If a man marries a woman, and after sleeping with her comes to hate her,
and he makes up charges against her and gives her a bad name, saying, "I married this woman, but when I came to her I did not find proof of her virginity,"
then the young woman's father and mother shall bring the proof of her virginity to the elders of the city at the gate.
The young woman's father shall say to the elders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he has come to hate her.

Now he has made up charges against her, saying, 'I did not find proof of your daughter's virginity.' But here is the proof of my daughter's virginity." Then her parents shall spread out the cloth before the elders of the city.
The elders of that city shall take the man and punish him.

They shall fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give them to the young woman's father, because he has given an Israelite virgin a bad name. She shall remain his wife, and he may never divorce her as long as he lives.
But if the charge is true, and no proof of the young woman's virginity is found,

she shall be brought to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death, because she has done a disgraceful thing in Israel by acting like a prostitute while in her father's house. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
If a man is found sleeping with another man's wife, both of them shall die, the man who slept with her and the woman as well. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.
If a man comes upon a virgin in the city who is engaged to another man, and he sleeps with her,

versions.text: If a virgin who is engaged to a man is met by another man in the city and he sleeps with her,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is active ("a man finds her in the city"), and the surrounding verses (25, 28) also use the active construction "if the man meets...". The passive "is met by another man" is heavier to read aloud and breaks the rhythm of the parallel case laws.

text: you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city and stone them to death—the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
But if the man meets the engaged young woman out in the open country, and he forces her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.

versions.text: But if the man meets the engaged young woman out in the country, and he seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb here (heḥeziq) denotes overpowering or forcing, which is the basis for the ruling that follows in verses 26–27; "seizes" alone is weaker. "Open country" also renders the field/countryside setting more clearly for oral reading.

text: Do nothing to the young woman; she has committed no sin deserving death. This case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and murders him.
For he found her out in the country, and though the engaged young woman cried out, there was no one to rescue her.
If a man meets a virgin who is not engaged, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered,
the man who lay with her shall give her father fifty pieces of silver, and she shall become his wife, because he has violated her. He may never divorce her as long as he lives.
